findings.claim: New statement in the 'Who points at whom' caption: 'lead_id points at another instructor, the person's team lead, so within one INSERT a lead's row comes before the rows that point at it.' The 'so' presents this as a foreign-key requirement, and it is not one. These ordinary (NOT DEFERRABLE) foreign keys are checked at the end of each statement, so the row order inside one multi-row INSERT does not matter: INSERT INTO instructors (instructor_id, name, lead_id) VALUES (2, 'Tomas', 1), (1, 'Mara', NULL); succeeds. The page's own simulator agrees (INSERT 0 2 on empty tables). The sentence also contradicts the page's correct rule two lines above ('These foreign keys are checked as each INSERT finishes'), and it teaches the wrong checking model just before Activity 2 asks learners to reason about it. Server outcome follows from the documented rule; not executed.

evidence.section: PostgreSQL 19 (current): SET CONSTRAINTS, Description: "IMMEDIATE constraints are checked at the end of each statement" and of the three classes, NOT DEFERRABLE: "The third class is always IMMEDIATE"

findings.recommendation: Drop the clause, or make it true and optional: 'lead_id points at another instructor, the person's team lead; a lead's row can come in the same INSERT, because the key is checked when the whole statement finishes.'

items.note: The footer no longer claims a PostgreSQL 18 server comparison; it says the editor's runs on this page were not repeated on a live server.
